What the KCDW gust model learned

Median (p50) model of the true 1-hour peak gust: 500 trees, 270 inputs, 190,470 training hours. Attributions are exact TreeSHAP on 40,000 random hours. Every prediction starts at the average, 11.03 kt, and each input pushes it up or down.

Which models it listens to

Average absolute push on the gust forecast, summed over each model's inputs. GEFS and WeatherNext 2 cover the whole 2021–2026 record, so the trees lean on them; ECMWF ensemble (2024 onward) and the short-archive models get less credit partly because they are missing in older hours.

Every hour, every input (beeswarm)

One dot per forecast hour (3,000 random hours), for the 15 inputs with the most influence. Position: how far that input pushed the gust forecast. Colour: the input's own value, as a percentile. low middle high model not available that hour.

The inputs that matter most

Low-level instability from GEFS is the single largest input, ahead of any wind speed. Ensemble medians beat single-run winds.

How each input moves the forecast

Line: average effect on the gust forecast at that input value. Band: 10th–90th percentile of the effect across hours (it depends on the other inputs).

The day's shape

Mean over the sample, by local hourobservedmodel median

The median sits ~0.4 kt under the observed mean at every hour, as it should: gusts are right-skewed, so the median is below the mean.

The first tree

Tree 1 of 500, top three levels (hover for exact thresholds). Wind speeds are m/s, sunshine W/m². Each later tree fixes what the earlier ones got wrong, in 0.05-sized steps.
